issue.title: Makefile: fix wrong C++ version suffix [rebase 2]

repository.name: grpc
repository.description: C++ based gRPC (C++, Python, Ruby, Objective-C, PHP, C#)

issue.body:
The C++ library files should have the suffix `-1` for 1.7.x instead of `-5` for 5.0.x of the C library files.

This fixes linking errors when using the library such as:
`error while loading shared libraries: libgrpc++.so.1: cannot open
shared object file: No such file or directory`

This is #12511 rebased on master. (Closes #12511).

This should fix #10299 and #12979.

issue.title: error while loading shared libraries: libgrpc++.so.1 in grpc 1.12.1

repository.name: grpc
repository.description: C++ based gRPC (C++, Python, Ruby, Objective-C, PHP, C#)

issue.body:
### What version of gRPC and what language are you using?
gRPC 1.12.1  /   C++ 
 
### What operating system (Linux, Windows, …) and version?
 CentOS Linux release 7.3.1611
 
### What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g. python version or version of gcc)
 gcc version 4.8.5
 
### What did you do?
When I run the program after compiling the example project code given in gRPC repo, it shows error while loading shared libraries.

some problem like [#10299](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/issues/10299)

### What did you see instead?
 ```
$ ./route_guide_server
./route_guide_server: error while loading shared libraries: libgrpc++.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```
What I have in `/usr/local/lib` are:
```sh
$/usr/local/lib    ll | grep libgrpc++.so
lrwxrwxrwx. 1 root root   19 Jun 12 10:27 libgrpc++.so -> libgrpc++.so.1.12.1
-rwxr-xr-x. 1 root root 378K Jun 12 10:27 libgrpc++.so.1.12.1
lrwxrwxrwx. 1 root root   19 Jun 12 10:27 libgrpc++.so.6 -> libgrpc++.so.1.12.1
```
```sh
$/usr/local/lib     ll | grep libgrpc.so
lrwxrwxrwx. 1 root root   16 Jun 12 10:26 libgrpc.so -> libgrpc.so.6.0.0
lrwxrwxrwx. 1 root root   16 Jun 12 10:26 libgrpc.so.6 -> libgrpc.so.6.0.0
-rwxr-xr-x. 1 root root 2.5M Jun 12 10:26 libgrpc.so.6.0.0
```
 The C++ so lib should be `libgrpc++.so.1` instead of `libgrpc++.so.6`,It seems like install file mismatch the `libgrpc.so` version to `libgrpc++.so` version.

### Anything else we should know about your project / environment?
Creating the symlink manually fixes the problem (but I haven't checked if grpc actually works).

issue.title: Fix invalid version .so links in Makefile

labels.name: release notes: yes
labels.description: Indicates if PR needs to be in release notes

repository.name: grpc
repository.description: C++ based gRPC (C++, Python, Ruby, Objective-C, PHP, C#)

issue.body:
The links to the .so files previously used a `${settings.core_version.major}` suffix for C, C++ and C#, which is incorrect.
Instead append the core major version for C, the cpp major version for C++ and the csharp major version for C# links.

This fixes an "error while loading shared libraries .. cannot open shared object file.." on an embedded Linux application which was linked dynamically to libgrpc++.

body:
I just merged https://github.com/grpc/grpc/pull/16832 which should fix the problem. The good news is this we made it on time for the v1.17.x branch cut so the fix is going to be available in the v1.17.0 release (coming in about two weeks).

Sorry it took so long, we are trying our best to review things on time, but this time we really screwed up by failing to address 3 separate PRs for the same issue. I think partially the problem was coming from the fact that we are maintaining multiple build systems and each one is pretty complex (and requires a specific knowledge set that not everyone on the team has), so engineers on the team are careful in accepting build system changes (that have the potential to break lots of things and aren't always easy to test). We are thinking of how we can improve the process so things like this don't happen again.
